clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy 2-year-old boy with incomplete immunizations presented with drowsiness, fever, vomiting, and loose stools. Initial examination revealed drowsiness (GCS 10-11), low-grade fever, tachycardia, hypotension, and slow pupillary reaction, but no meningeal signs. Initial blood tests showed leukopenia, high CRP, very high procalcitonin, coagulopathy, and high lactate. Antibiotics were administered, followed by a head CT showing mild diffuse cerebral edema. On day 2, a lumbar puncture (LP) revealed CSF findings consistent with bacterial meningitis (high protein, low glucose, very high WBC with polys, Gram-negative coccobacilli). An MRI on day 2 showed meningeal enhancement. Blood cultures (on admission) and CSF cultures confirmed beta-lactamase-negative ampicillin-resistant (BLNAR) Haemophilus influenzae type b meningitis, susceptible to ceftriaxone, meropenem, and cefotaxime. Initial treatment included intravenous ceftriaxone and dexamethasone. On day 7, the child was still febrile, and a second blood culture showed BLNAR H. influenzae resistant to ceftriaxone but sensitive to meropenem. The antibiotic was changed to meropenem, and the patient responded well, becoming afebrile.
